booleans:
# the two values of the type bool
print(type(True), type(False))
# they behave like 1 and 0 in arithmetic
print(True + True, int(False), True == 1)
# bool() turns a number into a Boolean value
print(bool(0), bool(1), bool(-3.5))
comparison:
x, y = 7, 9
# each comparison returns True or False
print(x == y, x != y, x < y)
print(x <= y, x > y, x >= y)
equality:
# a number and a string never fit each other
print(42 == 42.0, 42 == '42', 'hello' == 'Hello')
# decimals are stored in binary; strings follow character codes
print(0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3, 'apple' < 'banana', 'Z' < 'a')
chained:
age = 15
# 10 < age < 20 means 10 < age and age < 20
print(10 < age < 20, 10 < age < 12)
# every link of the chain must be true
print(1 < 2 > 1.5, 3 > 2 > 5)
notprec:
# not flips a value
print(not True, not False, not not True)
# not binds weaker than ==; and binds tighter than or
print(not 4 == 5, True or False and False)
# parentheses change the order
print((True or False) and False, not (True and False))
mixing:
age, member = 25, True
# comparisons first, Boolean operators after
print(age >= 18 and member)
print(age < 13 or age > 65)
print(not (age >= 18 and member))
shortcircuit:
# the division by zero is never reached
print(1 or 1 / 0, 0 and 1 / 0)
print('hi' and 'there', '' or 'default')
# the result is the last operand looked at
print(0 or [] or None, 1 and 2 and 3)
truthiness:
values = [0, 1, 0.0, '', 'a', [], [0], None]
for v in values:
    print(repr(v), bool(v))
# never write == True; test the value itself
greeting = 'hello'
print(greeting == True, bool(greeting))
block:
age = 70
if age > 65:
    print('senior')
    print('discount')
print('end')
indent:
x = 1
if x > 3:
    print('big')
    print('inside the block')
print('outside the block')
condexpr:
# a value if a condition else another value
for n in (7, 10):
    print(n, 'even' if n % 2 == 0 else 'odd')
# only the chosen side is evaluated
print('adult' if 20 >= 18 else 1 / 0)
match:
for status in (200, 403, 418):
    match status:
        case 200:
            print(status, 'ok')
        case 401 | 403 | 404:
            print(status, 'not allowed')
        case _:
            print(status, 'other')
